EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  March 26, 2018

CALL TO ORDER
CHAIRMAN MITCHELL called the meeting to order, the time being 7:00 p.m. in the Rolling
Hills Estates City Council Chambers.

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT
Chairman Judy Mitchell
Susan Brtis
Bill Kemp
Lou Persichina
Vicki Shinn
Carrie Silvano

STAFF MEMBER PRESENT
Andy Clark, Community Services Director

DRAFT MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 26, 2018
MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER KEMP

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE FEBRUARY 26, 2018 ADJOURNED
  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL SO ORDERED.

AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA
None.

CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICE COMPANY WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT MONTHLY
UPDATE
CHAIRMAN MITCHELL asked if any Committee Members had any questions about the
Neighborhood Outreach Committee meeting notes from February 28, 2018. Neighborhood
Outreach Committee Representative, MEMBER SILVANO, reported how impressed she was
by California Water Service Company’s outreach efforts and willingness to work with all
parties affected by the upcoming project.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
MARCH 26, 2018  1
 Audience member, Christine Wolf from 10 Lariat Lane, reported that her family was not happy
with alternate boarding impacts that they will face for several months during the project. She
reported that she inspected the Palos Verdes Stables, which recently became available, and
determined that this would be too far for her family members to ride to and from. Therefore,
she had reported to Nancy Wildman that her family’s horses would prefer to be boarded at the
Peter Weber Equestrian Center (PWEC).  Neighborhood Outreach Committee
Representative, MEMBER SHINN, stated that she will inform California Water Service
Company of the concerns that residents on the east side of the City have about moving their
horses to the Palos Verdes Stables at the upcoming May 23, 2018 committee meeting.

Nancy Wildman, 34 Pony Lane, RHE who is providing consulting services for California Water
Service Company regarding the temporary relocation of horses from her neighborhood,
reported that after meeting with all the horse owners who will be affected by the project, that
she had prepared a spreadsheet showing 19 were interested in going to PWEC, 5 may go to
Palos Verdes Stables, and 1 had an opportunity to board at The Empty Saddle Club. She
emphasized that California Water Service Company was very aware of how disruptive this
project will be to the entire community, but that there was no way around it in order to
complete this vital project.

In response to an inquiry, Ms. Wildman responded that the project would likely start in
September or October and take approximately five months to complete. Further, that Gil
Houle had submitted a barn construction company bid to California Water Service Company
and was negotiating their desired modifications to the proposed temporary pipe corrals
installation project. Finally, she suggested that the City consider widening the east fork of the
Phillips Canyon Trail to provide a secondary access route to those boarding near the Rolling
Hills Little League area, which could reduce the number of horse owners needing to be
relocated during the project and provide an additional escape route in case of an emergency
or should the Little League road ever have to be closed.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THE
MEETING NOTES.

DRAFT TRAIL SAFETY PAMPHLET
The Community Services Director reported that Sharon Yarber, PVP Horsemens Association
representative and Adrienne Mohan, PVP Land Conservancy Conservation Director met with
staff to begin developing content for a Trail Safety pamphlet to place at certain locations on
the City’s bridle/hiking trails. It was noted that there may be so much content regarding how to
safely share trails with equestrians, reporting trail safety conditions, dealing with trail
emergencies, and information about dangerous animals, insects and plants that there may be
a need for 2 or more pamphlets. A draft pamphlet is expected to be ready for the
Committee’s review at the April 2018 meeting.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
MARCH 26, 2018  2
 CHANDLER PARK ARENA RECREATIONAL RIDING PERIODS, TURNOUTS AND
LUNGING PERIODS

MEMBER SILVANO reported that the Horse Trainers have been monitoring the weekend
recreational riding-only periods from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. and have observed very little use
since the rule was implemented a few years ago.

Discussion ensued by the Committee and audience members regarding limiting, cancelling, or
changing this time period. It was noted that during the warmer summer months that many
recreational riders prefer to ride their horse earlier in the day versus around the mid-day
periods.

MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO CHANGE THE RECREATIONAL RIDING-ONLY HOURS TO 7:00 A.M. TO 9:00
  A.M. ON WEEKENDS AND NATIONAL HOLIDAYS FROM JUNE THROUGH
  AUGUST.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL SO ORDERED.

The Community Services Director stated that staff strongly recommends, for the sake of the
Chandler Park arena’s recently renovated base material and GGT footing, to continue to
enforce the no lunging or turnouts in this arena, noting that the Pepperwood Park round pen
should be used for these purposes. MEMBER SILVANO reported that turning out of horses
was continuing to periodically occur on weekends and that the City’s Code Enforcement staff
schedules should be adjusted to monitor this arena on weekends. MEMBER SHINN
indicated that she was aware of horse owners in her neighborhood who turned out their
horses at dusk or in the dark in this arena.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL SO ORDERED THAT THE NO
TURNOUTS AND LUNGING RULE REMAIN IN EFFECT FOR CHANDLER PARK ARENA.

EQUESTRIAN FEES
The Community Services Director reviewed the current Horse Trainer Permit, Horse Show,
Clinic, Dog Show, and Barn Rental fees and when they were last increased. In response to
an inquiry the Community Services Director, he indicated that there had not been substantial
operational cost increases over the past few years, but there had been large capital
expenditures from grant funds to improve the arenas and horse show booths at Ernie Howlett
Park. CHAIRMAN MITCHELL noted that the non-profit equestrian organizations, which hold
horse shows in the Howlett Park equestrian center, do not generate large surpluses of funds
from their annual horse show series.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THE
STAFF REPORT.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
MARCH 26, 2018  3
 PROPOSED HORSE CENSUS
The Community Services Director stated that a horse census, including potentially a horse
trailers census, was being discussed at the City’s General Plan Committee meetings.
MEMBER SILVANO, who is a member of this Committee, confirmed that it was under
consideration and could potentially assist with developing City emergency response
measures.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THE
STAFF REPORT.

PROPOSED NEW HORSE ARENA IN CHANDLER PARK
The Community Services Director reviewed past efforts in 2005 and 2016 to consider the
construction of another horse arena in Chandler Park. MEMBER SILVANO indicated that the
increase of boarding units at nearby Peter Weber Equestrian Center has increased use of the
Chandler Park arena. CHAIRMAN MITCHELL suggested that the Palos Verdes Landfill be
considered as an alternate location for an arena. MEMBER SHINN reminded the Committee
that the proposed dressage arena that had been previously discussed, just outside the west
end of the PWEC on the PV Landfill, was no longer being contemplated due to concerns
received from the adjacent Roanwood HOA neighborhood about potential dust and noise
issues.

The Community Services Director stated that if the Committee wanted to re-consider the
construction of a new arena in Chandler Park that their recommendation would need to be
reviewed by the Park and Activities Commission. He noted that a similar protocol would likely
be followed whereby the nearby neighborhoods around Chandler Park would be surveyed
again and that there was a 67% response against constructing a second arena in Chandler
Park in 2005. While not a busy park, he indicated that it is considered by some residents as
the City’s unofficial dog park. CHAIRMAN MITCHELL reported that City Council had recently
discussed the need for another dog park on the Palos Verdes Peninsula and that a letter to
LA County Supervisor Hahn’s office had been sent recommending a public dog park on the
Palos Verdes Landfill. MEMBER SILVANO responded that she would be against a dog park
at that site as they tend to attract large numbers of dog owners travelling from long distances.

Discussion ensued by various Committee Members regarding the peak use times and the low
use times at the Chandler Park arena. MEMBER SHINN requested that staff look into the
temporary installation of a video surveillance camera in Chandler Park for a period of at least
30 days so that the level of arena use at all times of each day could be measured, before
further consideration of a new arena’s construction. The Community Services Director
responded that he would work with the City’s Administrative Services Director and bring back
information at the next Committee meeting.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
MARCH 26, 2018  4
 HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL SO ORDERED THAT STAFF PROVIDE
TEMPORARY VIDEO SURVEILLANCE INFORMATION FOR CHANDLER PARK AT THE
NEXT COMMITTEE MEETING.

DRAFT MAYOR’S BREAKFAST RIDE FLYER
The Community Services Director noted that a photo change would occur on the draft flyer
and asked whether the Committee had any additional additions or changes to the draft flyer.
Sean Martin, 2 Empty Saddle Road, recommended adding equestrian games from 11:00 a.m.
to 1:00 p.m. in Howlett Park Arena #2. Los Serranos Awards Circuit Coordinator, Becky
Martin, stated that she was agreeable to allowing the games since the City’s Maintenance
staff had agreed to groom the arenas afterwards for their horse show the following morning.
In addition, Mr. Martin suggested that a riders’ raffle drawing occur amongst only those who
rode on the Mayor’s Breakfast Ride. The Committee concurred with both additions to the
draft event flyer. Audience member, Nancy Wildman, indicated that these additional
incentives to ride in this event would be in the next PVPHA Dispatch and member email
reminders would be sent out.

CHAIRMAN MITCHELL reminded the Committee that the elected officials will be available for
any interested riders to meet them beginning at 8:30 a.m. next to the Chandler Park arena.
She requested that the Community Services Director purchase a container of coffee and
water bottles to place on a table next to the arena. MEMBER SHINN volunteered to purchase
horse cookies for interested riders.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL SO ORDERED THAT THE MAYORS
BREAKFAST RIDE FLYER BE REVISED AS DISCUSSED.

CITY CELEBRATION VENUE
The Community Services Director reported that the Park and Activities Commission tabled the
Equestrian Committee’s recommendation to change the 2018 City Celebration venue from
Ernie Howlett Park back to The Empty Saddle Club. Instead, they have directed their City
Celebration Subcommittee with meet on April 11, 2018 at 6:30 p.m. in The Empty Saddle
Club clubhouse with other interested parties to develop a recommendation to the
Commission. In addition to the three Commissioners, they have asked that representatives
from the Remember the Music Festival and Empty Saddle Club attend, along with a City
Council Member and up to four Equestrian Committee Members.

CHAIRMAN MITCHELL determined that she was unable to attend that evening and that
another Council Member would be selected by the Mayor. MEMBERS KEMP, SHINN, and
SILVANO stated that they would represent the Equestrian Committee at the City Celebration
Subcommittee meeting.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL SO ORDERED THAT THE MEMBERS
KEMP, SHINN, AND SILVANO SHALL REPRESENT THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE AT
THE CITY CELEBRATION SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING ON APRIL 11, 2018.
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
MARCH 26, 2018  5
 EQUINE EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS EVENT
MEMBER SHINN reported that over 100 local equestrians attended the March 24, 2018
Equine Emergency Workshop at Ernie Howlett Park. She reported that the information
presented was excellent, as they learned about the reverse 911 system, assembling equine
emergency “go bags”, and that LA County was willing to offer the Level 1 Equine Response
Training course on the PV Peninsula. MEMBER SILVANO, however, indicated that they
learned that there no central plan had yet been developed for equine emergencies or
evacuation responses on the Palos Verdes Peninsula.

At the encouragement of Committee Members, audience member Sean Martin reported that
he would develop a clinic on horse trailer maintenance and loading procedures. CHAIRMAN
MITCHELL asked for volunteers to work with City and County staff to assist in developing
equine emergency response procedures. MEMBERS KEMP and SHINN indicated interest
and the Community Services Director stated that he will put them in contact with the
appropriate City staff member.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL SO ORDERED THAT THE MEMBERS
KEMP AND SHINN FORM THE EQUINE EMERGENCY RESPONSE SUBCOMMITTEE.

EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG
HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

COMMITTEE MEMBER REPORTS
A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL REPORTS
  MEMBER KEMP reported that a PV Drive North Trail sign pole was down across from
  City Hall.

B.  ERNIE HOWLETT PARK JUMP POLES AND RAKES
  The Community Services Director reported that additional jump poles had been
  purchased and installed in Howlett Park’s Arena #1 in time for the upcoming horse
  show season. In addition, it was reported at the last Equestrian Committee meeting
  that the rakes used to remove horse manure from the Howlett Park arenas had been
  stolen. Staff was able to find them in other locations around the arenas. Audience
  member, Sean Martin suggested that more trash and recycle bins be placed around
  the arenas.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS
A.  PV PENINSULA WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT UPDATE – Monthly

B.  EQUINE EMERGENCY RESPONSE PLAN – Monthly

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
MARCH 26, 2018  6
 C.  TEMPORARY CAMERA AT CHANDLER PARK ARENA – April 23, 2018

D.  DRAFT TRAIL SAFETY PAMPHLET – April 23, 2018

E.  CITY CELEBRATION VENUE – April 23, 2018

F.  MAYOR’S BREAKFAST RIDE PROMOTIONS UPDATE – April 23, 2018

ADJOURNMENT
MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO ADJOURN THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL ADJOURNED THE MEETING.

The meeting adjourned at 8:36 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

Andy Clark
Community Services Director

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
MARCH 26, 2018  7
